key_audit_matters: Capitalization of Asset: The Company has continued to invest in storage terminals and warehousing infrastructure to support its Infrastructure segment operations. Determining the appropriate point of capitalisation of such assets — including allocation of direct and indirect costs, treatment of borrowing costs under Ind AS 23 on qualifying assets, and classification between Property, Plant and Equipment and Investment Property based on intended use — involves significant management judgment.

Evaluation of uncertain tax positions: The Company operates in multiple jurisdictions and is subject to periodic challenges by local tax authorities on a range of tax matters during the normal course of business including direct and indirect tax matters. These involve significant management judgment to determine the possible outcome of the uncertain tax positions, consequently having an impact on related accounting and disclosures in the financial statements.

outlook.statement: The performance of the Company is expected to improve in the year ahead in terms of enhanced capacity utilisation, efficient operations and better profitability as a result of above measures being taken.

Indian warehousing market projected to reach ~USD 40 billion by 2031 (CAGR 7-9%); renewable energy outlook favorable with wind generation expected to grow at 8.2% avg annual rate through 2030; liquid storage demand driven by petrochemical/chemical capacity expansion and port-led infrastructure development.

Company will selectively evaluate opportunities based on long-term PPAs, open access or assured power-sale arrangements; focus on maintaining existing wind assets, controlling theft/generation losses, improving operational performance; cautious and selective approach towards new wind capacity addition.

Warehousing business to remain focused on optimizing utilization of existing assets, diversifying customer base, strengthening operational efficiency and cost discipline, selectively pursuing capacity expansion and customized warehousing opportunities with disciplined approach guided by demand visibility, asset utilization potential, customer commitment, expected returns and commercial viability.
The Company has continued to invest in storage terminals and warehousing infrastructure to support its Infrastructure segment operations.

risks: Depreciation charged and impairment expenses (including write offs) have been the main reasons for inadequate profits earned by the Company.
Loss in generation of wind energy due to operational and cable theft issues.
Government policy amendments in import/export policies
Development of new port infrastructure near existing ports
Operational hazards and risks
Natural disasters
Pandemic situations
Temporary vacancy or slower re-leasing in Tier-III warehouse locations due to smaller market size and limited customer base depth

Cost pressures from increase in construction/development costs (cement, steel, aluminum, labour, diesel, equipment rentals, plumbing/electrical fixtures) not matched by proportional rental rate increases in Tier-III markets
Wind energy business operating at lower utilisation due to theft incidents at project sites
Transmission and grid constraints in renewable energy
Tariff and competitive pressure in renewable energy
Intermittency and energy storage requirements
Equipment and technology risks
Policy and regulatory changes
Increasing competition from solar and hybrid projects
Core business of storage infrastructure and renewable energy not prone to commodity price risk/foreign exchange risk
Entire equity shareholding of promoter group not in demat form (non-compliance with Regulation 31(2) of Listing Regulations)
